record.paper_title: Banach spaces and Ramsey Theory: some open problems
record.original_question: Does every Banach space of density strictly greater than ℵ_1 have a support set?

evidence.quote: Problem 19. (S. Todorcevic [79]) Does every Banach space of density > ℵ1 have a support set?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $X$ be an infinite-dimensional Banach space. The density of $X$, denoted $\mathrm{dens}(X)$, is the least cardinality of a norm-dense subset of $X$. A subset $S \subseteq X$ is called a support set if $S$ is convex and every point of $S$ is a support point of $S$ — that is, for every $x \in S$ there exists a continuous linear functional $f \in X^*$ with $f \neq 0$ on $S$ such that $f(x) = \inf_{y \in S} f(y)$ (equivalently, $S$ has a supporting hyperplane through $x$).

Question: Does every Banach space $X$ with $\mathrm{dens}(X) > \aleph_1$ contain a support set?
artifact.status_search_result: Todorcevic constructed (in "Biorthogonal systems and quotient spaces via Baire category methods", Math. Ann. 2006) a generic Banach space $C(K)$ of density $\aleph_1$ with no support set, motivating the question for densities above $\aleph_1$. A targeted web search did not return a published resolution of the question for densities strictly greater than $\aleph_1$; the problem appears to still be open, but no definitive recent statement was found, so the status is recorded as unknown.

status_evidence.title: Biorthogonal systems and quotient spaces via Baire category methods
status_evidence.snippet: Todorcevic constructs a generic C(K) Banach space of density ℵ_1 with no support set.
status_evidence.claim: Establishes that the analogous statement fails at density ℵ_1, motivating the open question above ℵ_1.
